chunks: Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said:
We were in Medina, so he sent a message to us: 'Prepare for us Falouzaj, and make only a little.' So we sent it to him in a small bowl.

key_terms.الْمَدِينَةِ: Medina, the city where the event took place
key_terms.فَالُوذَجَ: A type of sweet drink or confection mentioned in the hadith
key_terms.قَصْعَةٍ: A shallow bowl or dish used for serving food or drink

ai.seo_question: What is Falouzaj and how did the Imam consume it?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the cultural practice of sharing sweets as a means of social bonding and hospitality in early Shia communities. The specific request for 'Falouzaj' (a sweetened drink or confection) and the modest serving vessel underscore the Imam’s preference for simplicity and accessibility, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on humility in daily interactions. It serves as a practical example of how religious leaders engaged with their followers in informal, everyday settings, fostering closeness and community spirit.

en.hubeali:
Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘We were at Al-Medina, so heasws sent a message to us to make Falouzaj (a sweet drink) for himasws, and make only a little. So we sent it over to himasws in a small bowl’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ibn Faddal has narrated from Yunus ibn Ya’qub who has said the following: “

We were in al-Madinah and abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, sent a message to us to make for him (the Imam) Faludah (a kind of sweet) of a little quantity . We then sent it to him (the Imam) in a small bowl.’”
